introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 2 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: three hours.**

Answer ALL 10 questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated. Mathematical formulae and tables published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
incertitudes: Sujet scanné sans figure imprimée. Les points imprimés sont des totaux approximatifs par partie, entre crochets ; le sujet n'imprime aucun total par question, donc le champ points de l'exercice est vide.

Question 7 (iii) : le sujet demande le « radius » de la similitude ; le corrigé l'interprète comme son rapport (module du multiplicateur), égal à 2. Le sujet écrit « Determinethe » (coquille d'impression) : recopié « Determine the ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
A transformation, $f$, on a complex plane is defined by $z' = 2z + 3 - 4i$.

Find the image of the point $z = 2 - i$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Substitute $z = 2 - i$:

$$z' = 2(2 - i) + 3 - 4i = 4 - 2i + 3 - 4i = 7 - 6i.$$

$$\boxed{z' = 7 - 6i}$$

that is, the point $(7, -6)$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A transformation, $f$, on a complex plane is defined by $z' = 2z + 3 - 4i$.

Determine the invariant point of $f$ in the form $a + ib$, $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An invariant point satisfies $z' = z$:

$$z = 2z + 3 - 4i \;\Longrightarrow\; -z = 3 - 4i \;\Longrightarrow\; z = -3 + 4i.$$

$$\boxed{z = -3 + 4i}$$

that is, the point $(-3, 4)$.

**Check.** $2(-3 + 4i) + 3 - 4i = -6 + 8i + 3 - 4i = -3 + 4i$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A transformation, $f$, on a complex plane is defined by $z' = 2z + 3 - 4i$.

Show that $f$ is a similarity transformation (similitude), stating its radius.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $\omega = -3 + 4i$ be the invariant point. Subtracting $\omega = 2\omega + 3 - 4i$ from $z' = 2z + 3 - 4i$ gives

$$z' - \omega = 2(z - \omega).$$

More generally, for any two points $z_1, z_2$ with images $z_1', z_2'$:

$$z_1' - z_2' = 2(z_1 - z_2) \;\Longrightarrow\; |z_1' - z_2'| = 2\,|z_1 - z_2|.$$

Every distance is multiplied by the same constant, $2$, and $z \mapsto az + b$ with $a \neq 0$ also preserves angles (it multiplies every difference $z_1 - z_2$ by the same complex number $a = 2$). So $f$ is a similarity transformation (similitude), of **ratio (the "radius" of the similitude) $2$**; since $\arg 2 = 0$, its angle is $0$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A transformation, $f$, on a complex plane is defined by $z' = 2z + 3 - 4i$.

Give the geometrical interpretation of $f$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
From $z' - \omega = 2(z - \omega)$ with $\omega = -3 + 4i$: the multiplier $2$ is real and positive, so there is no rotation.

$$\boxed{f \text{ is the enlargement (homothety) with centre } (-3, 4), \text{ that is } -3 + 4i, \text{ and scale factor } 2.}$$

Each point is mapped to the point on the same ray from the centre, at twice the distance.
